title: Letter and Regiment
premise: In 1917, apprentice clockmaker Ansel Galloway is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock and finds a child abandoned at its door with a note: forget the face. The child carries letters implicating Colonel Merrick Vane—Ansel's estranged uncle—in falsifying casualty rolls to sell soldiers' berths home before the armistice. As Vane's men close in, Ansel must decide whether to expose the truth and destroy the only family they have left, or stay silent as the innocent are erased. In the end, Ansel repairs the clock to chime the armistice hour publicly, forcing the letters into the open; Vane falls, and Ansel keeps the child, choosing a family made rather than inherited.
about_author: Ansel Blackwood is the pen name of a former horologist's apprentice who spent a decade restoring church tower clocks across northern England. Their fiction draws on the quiet violence of small towns and the machinery of secrets kept too long.

chapters.title: The Hour That Would Not Strike
chapters.summary: Ansel Galloway arrives at the observatory to repair the stalled master clock, navigating a town that has learned not to look at them. Inside, they find a child asleep among the gears with a satchel of sealed letters. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: wary curiosity curdling into dread—the first crack in seven years of practiced invisibility.

chapters.title: Instructions in a Dead Man's Hand
chapters.summary: The satchel holds a dying soldier's letters naming Colonel Merrick Vane—Ansel's mother's brother—as selling homebound berths and striking dead men from the rolls. The child, Wren, cannot say who left her. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the sick recognition that silence, their old craft, has been someone else's weapon.

chapters.title: What the Family Kept Polished
chapters.summary: Ansel visits Uncle Vane under the pretense of family duty, finding a man gilded by medals and grief, who warns them gently about 'troublemakers at the observatory.' POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: love and suspicion tangled—the horror of realizing charm can be inventory for corruption.

chapters.title: A Watch That Loses No Time
chapters.summary: Vane's adjutant, Sergeant Hale, begins shadowing Ansel, buying bread from their shop, asking after the child. Ansel hides Wren with the observatory's blind caretaker, Mrs. Odell. POV: alternating Ansel and Hale. Emotional beat: claustrophobic surveillance; Hale's own doubts surface—he lost a brother to a falsified roll.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Ansel deciphers the letters fully: names, payments, dates—one berth per signature, the last berth reserved for the armistice eve transport. Among the sold names is Mrs. Odell's son, listed dead though he lives. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into purpose; justice must come from outside the law that wrote the lie.

chapters.title: Blood Is a Currency
chapters.summary: Vane confronts Ansel privately, offering legitimacy, the family name restored, if the letters burn. He reveals he knows about Wren. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging—Ansel nearly accepts, then sees Wren's chalk drawing of them on the workshop wall.

chapters.title: Rust in the Escapement
chapters.summary: Hale, torn, tips Ansel off that the observatory will be searched at dawn. Ansel smuggles Wren out through the clock tower's weights while Hale 'fails' to find the satchel. POV: alternating Ansel and Hale. Emotional beat: fragile alliance between two people complicit in different silences.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Vane accelerates the plan: the final berth on the armistice-eve transport, and he offers it to Ansel—for themselves or the child, but only one, and only with the letters destroyed. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the cruelest choice sharpened to a single point; loyalty and truth finally demand opposite answers.

chapters.title: Eleven O'Clock
chapters.summary: Climax. On armistice morning, Ansel finishes repairing the master clock so it strikes eleven publicly, reading the letters aloud from the tower as the town gathers below and the bells carry the names over the parade ground. Vane orders Hale to stop him; Hale refuses. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: terror becoming clarity—the moment staying invisible ends forever.

chapters.title: Keeping Time
chapters.summary: Vane is arrested by his own officers as the armistice bells fade; the sold names are restored to the rolls, including Odell's son, who comes home. Ansel declines restitution, takes guardianship of Wren, and winds the master clock each week. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—not innocence recovered, but a chosen family and a truth that finally keeps time.
